sources.entry: Syncthing - Syncthing is an open source peer-to-peer file synchronisation tool. (Source Code) MPL-2.0 Go/Docker/deb

summary.one_liner: Syncthing is an open source, continuous peer-to-peer file synchronization program that keeps files in sync between two or more computers.
summary.what_it_does: Syncthing synchronizes files continuously between two or more computers. The README states its priorities in order: safety from data loss, security against eavesdropping and modification, ease of use, automation, broad platform availability, and focus on individual users. It provides a graphical interface through several GUI implementations for Windows, Mac, and Linux, according to the README. Example configurations are included for running it in the background as a service. A Docker setup is documented separately. Release binaries are GPG-signed, with a built-in ECDSA-signed automatic upgrade mechanism that some distribution channels disable. macOS and Windows binaries are code-signed. Building from source uses `go run build.go`, and the documentation lives on a separate documentation site.
use_cases: sync files between my own computers
peer-to-peer file sharing without a central server
run a background file sync service on Linux, Mac, or Windows
how_to_run: Binaries are created in ./bin after building from source
See the getting started guide in the Syncthing documentation site
Use the example service files in the etc directory to keep Syncthing running in the background
To run in Docker, see the Docker README linked from the project
notable: Peer-to-peer design with no central server required, per the README's description of peer-to-peer synchronization
Signed releases: GPG-signed binaries plus a compiled-in ECDSA signature for automatic upgrades
Goals document ranks data-loss safety and security above all other concerns
Several third-party GUI implementations for Windows, Mac, and Linux
caveats: Automatic upgrade mechanism is disabled in some distribution channels
Feature details, supported platforms, and setup steps are on the separate documentation site, not in this README
